subject: URGENT: Persistent p99 spikes and 500s during peak — suspected KV hotkey thrash
messages:
From: Ethan Kim <ethan.kim@northbridge.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Ross <claire.ross@northbridge.ai>
Date: 2026-12-15T08:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production tail latency / 500s spike — urgent

Connor —

We're seeing sustained p99 increases (from ~450ms to 2.2s) and a burst of 500 responses across our tenant between 07:00-09:30 PST this morning. The spike correlates with our daily ingestion window but the pattern looks like repeated cache invalidations — several thousand cache misses in a minute followed by a flood of backend calls.

This started after the model rollout yesterday (small weights change) but support told us this looks like the KV layer thrashing. Our app times out and we lost several morning-critical requests. We need immediate mitigation: either a short-term traffic reroute or capacity bump. We also need ownership confirmation and an ETA for a fix.

I've attached a small sample of the 500 responses and request traces. Please advise ASAP — this is customer-impacting for our sales team that demo this morning.

Thanks,
Ethan
Head of Platform, Northbridge Analytics

Attachments: nbridge-500-samples.zip (20KB)

Immediate plan: Naomi & ops will triage traces and try an emergency mitigation (reduce batching, pause prefetch, and temporarily lower tenant priority). If that doesn't rapidly restore p99 we can failover your traffic to a reserved Dedicated pool for the next 2 hours while we stabilize.

I'll keep you updated every 30 minutes until the issue is closed. Can you confirm whether the ingestion burst was a scheduled job (time-of-day) or a one-off replay? That helps us tune prefetch windows.

Connor

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-12-15T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production tail latency / 500s spike — urgent

Connor — quick summary from initial triage (ops findings attached as a playback trace):

- Root symptoms: sudden surge of single-key lookups for a small set (~3) of keys, causing frequent evictions and synchronous backend reads. We observed HOL-style blocking on server workers while they waited on KV fills.
- Metrics: cache miss rate spiked from 2% -> 48% across the tenant; slot eviction churn increased 12x; average backend latency per fill ~380ms.
- Correlation: the spike started ~07:04 PST, immediately after a large batch ingestion job from NB that includes per-customer metadata tags (confirmed by their trace ids).

Immediate mitigations we've applied (live now):
1) Disabled background prefetch for Northbridge for the next 90 minutes.
2) Reduced default batch-size from 64 -> 12 for Northbridge route to lower HOL headroom.
3) Increased per-tenant soft cache quota by +30% on a best-effort basis to reduce eviction churn.
4) Activated emergency fallback: requests that hit a hotkey and exceed 1s now route to model-variant-compact (slightly higher latency but stable).

Preliminary effect: p99 has dropped to ~720ms from 2.2s in the last 12 minutes; 500s have fallen by ~85% in sampled traces. We're continuing to monitor.

Next steps (24-72h):
- We need to revisit the tenant's KV allocation profile: either pin hotkeys to a reserved slot set or add admission controls at the router to smooth ingestion bursts.
- Karthik and Jonas to propose a config diff (eviction policy + prefetch window + soft quota) and run a canary tonight.
- Connor / Marissa to coordinate messaging and whether a temporary Dedicated lane is warranted.

I've attached the playback trace (playback-trace-XY12.json) and a snapshot of the KV metrics. I'll follow up with a short runbook for preventatives.

Naomi Feldman
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: playback-trace-XY12.json, kv-cache-metrics-20261215.png

If a paid Dedicated bump is necessary we'll sign whatever is needed; prefer an automated short-term toggle so we don't need manual ops each day.

Ethan
